notes: Account summary: Borealis is a fintech personalization platform with live chat, ranking, and indexing workloads. Heavy peak hours (US market open) with sustained bursts. Cost-sensitive but will pay for predictability and hard SLOs.
Primary objective: get a committed/dedicated pool that guarantees throughput and tail latency for chat while delivering predictable unit economics per token for forecasting.
Throughput & SLO targets: 10k rps small inference calls (embeddings/rerank batch), chat median latency <80ms, p95 <200ms, p99 <400ms for standard prompt lengths (<=512 tokens).
Preferred GPU types: leaning to H100-like for headroom; open to mixed pool with quantized variants for cost-sensitive background traffic.
Commit level options discussed (summary):
- Tier A (baseline): 6 reserved GPUs — assumes 60% utilization on peak baseline; targeted for steady-state chat + embeddings; estimated ARR mid-range.
- Tier B (recommended): 12 reserved GPUs — supports planned growth and headroom for spikes; amortized unit cost/token improves with utilization; includes burst credits to public pool.
- Tier C (aggressive): 24 reserved GPUs — enterprise commit with steep discount; requires 75%+ sustained utilization to meet unit-cost targets.
Cost modeling assumptions included in internal deck:
- Baseline token mix: 70% small chat messages (avg 40 tokens), 20% embeddings (avg 512 tokens), 10% reranking (multiple candidates).
- Scheduling/ batching: continuous batching with 20-40ms batching window for embeddings, adaptive batching for chat with priority lanes for low-latency requests.
- Quantization & model variants: 8-bit quantized rerank/embedding variants reduce GPU memory pressure and lower per-token cost by ~30% for background jobs.
- Cache hit assumptions: prefix/KV cache expected to give 12-18% token savings on repeat chat flows (session-based caching).
- Utilization curves: peak hours (4 hours/day) reach 80-95% utilization on reserved pool; off-peak 20-35% unless background jobs scheduled.
Unit economics presented to customer:
- Dedicated unit cost (illustrative): $0.0009/token at 70% effective utilization on Tier B H100 pool with quantization and caching considered.
- Hosted fallback cost: $0.0023/token for on-demand public models (used for overflow) — customers liked explicit delta for overflow routing policy.
- Break-even analysis: showed commit pays off vs on-demand when sustained utilization >45% and >9 months of steady load.
Operational & SLA negotiation points called out:
- Latency SLOs: define p95/p99 targets per route, with differential for embeddings vs chat. Need explicit measurement windows and instrumentation hooks (trace ids).
- Throughput guarantees: define requests/sec per reserved GPU baseline and how autoscaling/burst credits are applied during sustained spikes.
- Capacity planning: reserve mixed instance types or allow hot/cold pools; Borealis prefers predictable fixed capacity for PCI/PII handling.
- SLA credits: proposed sliding scale of credits for monthly uptime below 99.9%, and an additional credit if p99 latency exceeds negotiated threshold for >3 rolling days.
- Failover behavior: must ensure automatic fallback to approved smaller model (quantized) within 120s and route to hosted overflow with explicit data residency flags.
Customer quotes & impressions:
- "We need line-of-sight into cost per active session — not just token counts. If you can show predictable unit economics under peak, procurement will greenlight a two-year commit."
- "Latency tail behavior is our biggest worry — one bad 99th percentile event during pricing period could kill adoption."
Open technical action items (POC metrics to deliver):
- Deliver 48-hr sustained-run report with GPU utilization heatmap, tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies by route (chat vs embeddings).
- Produce detailed cost model spreadsheet (CSV link) with sensitivity to utilization, quantization level, and cache hit rate.
- Confirm KMS/HSM key wrapping and audit log retention policy; surface contract language for data residency.
Commercial action items:
- Finalize three-tier commit pricing with explicit burst credits and overage pricing per GPU-hour and per-token overflow rate.
- Draft proposed SLA clause with uptime credit schedule and performance-credit trigger for persistent tail latency regressions.

- (Diego) Attach POC artifact (48-hr run) into Drive and schedule post-POC review (2024-12-12).
